title: Protocol for analyzing antibody responses to glycoprotein antigens using electron-microscopy-based polyclonal epitope mapping
protocol: In BSC with proper personal protective equipment, combine 2 mL slurry and 1 mL serum in 15 mL conical tube.
Bring volume up to 5 mL with PBS.
Secure tube lid with parafilm.
Mix serum and resin for 1–3 days at 4°C.
Remove parafilm and centrifuge the mixture for 3 min at 3,200 × g.
Decant serum into 10% bleach.
Fill 15 mL tube with PBS, mix and centrifuge for 3 min at 3,200 × g, decant into 10% bleach.
Repeat washing step twice more.
Add 1 mL PBS to the resin-bound IgG.
Elute IgG from Protein G resin by adding 5 mL (5 CV) of 0.1 M Glycine pH 2.5 to the slurry.
Secure lid and incubate for 15 minutes at 20°C, gently mixing on rocker.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 3,200 × g.
Decant supernatant (IgG-containing) into 4 mL of 1 M Tris pH 8.
Filter elution into a new tube using a 0.2 μm pore filter to remove remaining resin beads.
Buffer exchange into PBS with a 30 or 100 kDa molecular cut-off 15 mL concentrator.
Spin down IgG-containing elution buffer.
Fill concentrator with PBS.
Spin down to reach a total volume of 0.5–1 mL.
Transfer IgG to a microcentrifuge tube.
Measure IgG concentration using an extinction coefficient of 13.7 A1% at 280 nm and calculate the total IgG.
Store IgG at 4°C for up to 2 weeks or store at -80°C indefinitely if not used immediately.
Activate papain according to the recipe provided in materials and equipment.
Combine 10× Tris/EDTA, 10× L-cysteine, isolated IgG, and PBS for a total of 9.8 ml (total reaction volume is 10 ml).
Add 200 μl activated papain to the mixture.
Incubate digestion reaction for 4–5 h at 37°C.
Quench reaction by adding 600 μl of 500 mM iodoacetamide (final concentration 30 mM).
Digest antibodies using papain, cysteine, and iodoacetamide.
Isolate polyclonal Fab along with the Fc region in size exclusion chromatography (SEC).
Collect undigested IgG before the Fab/Fc peak in SEC.
Separate Fab2′ shoulder that precedes the largest digested Fab peak in SEC.
Remove papain after the Fab/Fc peak in SEC.
Equilibrate the SEC column with PBS.
Add 15 μg of HIV Env to 250-500 μg of polyclonal Fab/Fc.
Incubate the complex overnight.
Inject polyclonal Fab/Fc digest sample onto SEC column and collect 500 μl per well using a 96 deep-well block.
Collect entire column volume.
Combine wells from largest peak corresponding to 50 kDa proteins.
Concentrate Fab/Fc to about 500 μl.
Add 0.025% sodium azide and store isolated Fab at 4°C for up to one month or at -80°C indefinitely if not used immediately.
Incubate complex overnight at 4°C.
Equilibrate SEC column (GE S200i) with TBS.
Inject complex and collect 500 μL per well using a 96 deep-well block.
Concentrate to about 200–500 μL.
Dilute with TBS as needed.
Add 0.025% sodium azide to prevent contamination growth.
Glow discharge grid at 15 mA for 25 s.
Place 2, 3 μL drops of UF onto parafilm.
Load 3 μL sample at a final concentration of 0.04 mg/mL onto grid.
Blot with filter paper.
Pick up UF droplet by blotting with grid.
Wait 10 seconds.
Blot with filter paper.
Wait 10 seconds and pick up second drop of UF.
Wait 50–60 seconds.
Blot with filter paper.
Image grid on the same day or screen for dilution and stain quality.
Collect negative stain EM data by loading grids onto an electron microscope equipped with LaB6 or FEG emission source and CCD camera.
Acquire micrographs in linear mode without motion correction, ensuring defocus range from −1.5 to −2.5 μm and total dose of about 25 e-/Å².
Collect enough micrographs for approximately 100,000 initial particles (typically 200-300 micrographs).
Import micrographs.
Skip CTF estimation for negative-stain data.
Pick particles using Laplacian-of-Gaussian autopicking and adjust the minimum diameter setting as necessary.
Ensure that “particles are white” is selected in the settings.
Decrease the minimum diameter if too few particles are picked, or increase it if background noise is excessive.
Extract particles without inverting contrast for negatively-stained samples.
Perform 2D classification (50–100 classes) using default RELION parameters.
Select 2D classes that resemble antigen with or without Fabs bound.
Troubleshoot issues following the provided guidance.
Perform another round of 2D classification (50–100 classes).
Choose 2D classes that best represent antigen.
Use a low-pass filtered ligand-free antigen as the initial model for 3D classification (25 classes) using default RELION parameters.
Ensure each class has at least 1000 input particles.
Select 3D classes that resemble antigen with Fab bound.

Repeat 3D classification jobs as needed to sort maps of Fabs bound to antigen, ensuring no more than 40 classes and each class has a sufficient number of input particles (greater than or equal to 1000).
Perform 3D refinements on the final selected classes from the 3D classification.
Using UCSF Chimera, isolate Fab volume from antigen with Segger tool.
Save desired segment.
Apply Gaussian filter.
Resample filtered volume on the grid of input map.
Save filtered and resampled volume.
Incubate antigen and polyclonal Fab overnight.
Purify the complex using size exclusion chromatography (SEC).
Prepare negative stain EM grids immediately after purification.
Conduct serum neutralization assays.
Perform enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for binding analysis.
